name: Question 5
problem:
A particle $P$ is traveling along the $x$-axis with displacement $s(t)$ from a fixed origin $O$ given by

$$
s(t)={t}^{2}ln\,({t}^{2}),\,t>0.
$$

Find the time at which the acceleration is zero, and find the value of the velocity at this moment.

The acceleration is zero at $t=$
{{field-1}}, and the velocity at this moment is
$v=$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
s(t)={t}^{2}ln\,({t}^{2})=2{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\,(2{t}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)) \\  & =2(2t)\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+2{t}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{t} \\  & =4t\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+2t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+2t) \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+4t\cdot \frac{1}{t}+2 \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+6\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we put $a(t)=0$ to find the time when the acceleration is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+6 & =0 \\ 4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t) & =-6 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(t) & =-\frac{3}{2} \\ t & ={e}^{-3/2}\end{aligned}
$$

So the acceleration is zero when $t={e}^{-3/2}.$ To find the velocity at this moment, we substitute this back into $v(t)$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}v\,({e}^{-3/2}) & ={e}^{-3/2}(4ln\,({e}^{-3/2})+2) \\  & ={e}^{-3/2}(4\cdot (-\frac{3}{2})+2) \\  & ={e}^{-3/2}(-6+2) \\  & =-4{e}^{-3/2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the acceleration is zero at $t={e}^{-3/2},$ and the velocity at this moment is $v=-4{e}^{-3/2}.$

EXPLANATION

First, we calculate v(t) by differentiating s(t):
s(t)=t2ln(t2)=2t2ln⁡(t)

v(t)=dsdt=ddt(2t2ln⁡(t))=2(2t)ln⁡(t)+2t2⋅1t=4tln⁡(t)+2t

Now, we differentiate v(t) to find a(t): a(t)=dvdt=ddt(4tln⁡(t)+2t)=4ln⁡(t)+4t⋅1t+2=4ln⁡(t)+6

Next, we put a(t)=0 to find the time when the acceleration is zero: 4ln⁡(t)+6=04ln⁡(t)=−6ln⁡(t)=−32t=e−3/2

So the acceleration is zero when t=e−3/2. To find the velocity at this moment, we substitute this back into v(t) to get v(e−3/2)=e−3/2(4ln(e−3/2)+2)=e−3/2(4⋅(−32)+2)=e−3/2(−6+2)=−4e−3/2

Therefore, the acceleration is zero at t=e−3/2, and the velocity at this moment is v=−4e−3/2.
